parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a pure Rust 2021 Cargo project, root `test11.rs`, exact CLI behavior, std-only implementation, byte-identical load-factor formatting, and oracle-based verification.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent probed the oracle, inferred the growth and formatting behavior, then made one coder child the implementation and verification owner while retaining parent-level acceptance checks.
parallel.implementation: The child wrote `Cargo.toml`, a root `hopscotch.rs` map simulator, and `test11.rs` with `std::stoi`-like parsing, f32 load-factor math, C++ `%g` formatting, and the required output sequence.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote directly into `/output`; the parent received the child summary, listed the final files, and ran the delivered `/output/test11` against selected oracle cases before final response.
parallel.verification: The child ran both `rustc` and cargo builds, a required differential loop, extra CLI cases, abort parity checks, and cargo-binary spot checks; the parent independently spot-checked seven cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No visible unfinished required work remained; the official evaluator completed and passed all 39 test cases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, exact CLI, exact formatting, black-box behavior inference, root entry file, and build/delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor performed all oracle probing, inferred thresholds, implemented the project, built binaries, ran differential tests, and wrote the final report without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/hopscotch_map.rs`, `src/cpp_fmt.rs`, and `test11.rs`, using a HashMap wrapper, threshold bookkeeping, exact f32 formatting, and `std::stoi`-compatible parsing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run assembled a Cargo project with a root binary target and src modules, produced `/output/test11` via rustc, and confirmed the non-target file layout.
serial.verification: The serial actor built with cargo and rustc, ran a broad differential harness over hundreds of valid and edge cases, then checked the cargo-built binary on representative arguments.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No visible unfinished required work remained; the official evaluator completed and passed all 39 test cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used the prompt requirements and parent probes to capture exact CLI, formatting, map-growth, project layout, and verification obligations before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and independently probed the oracle for the exact C++ behavior and edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage gap: both identified and implemented the same externally tested obligations; the parallel run encoded them in a child brief while serial kept them locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split work into parent oracle inference and a single coder child responsible for implementation, builds, differential tests, and reporting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main actor owned all inference, implementation, integration, and verification steps itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had one explicit delegation boundary but no ownership gap; serial had no boundary and no subagent activity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief included inferred bucket thresholds, formatting expectations, `std::stoi` semantics, exact file paths, build commands, and differential test obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor retained context internally, refining oracle observations directly into the implementation without any handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel transferred a rich interface and acceptance contract to one child; serial needed no handoff, and neither path shows a lost, stale, or conflicting interface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child created a compact project with `Cargo.toml`, `hopscotch.rs`, and root `test11.rs`, implementing the map simulator, parser, and formatter.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor created a Cargo project with `src/lib.rs`, `src/hopscotch_map.rs`, `src/cpp_fmt.rs`, and root `test11.rs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The layouts differed, but both implemented the same load-factor and formatting behavior and satisfied the evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child completed normally, returned a detailed summary, and the parent then ran its own spot-check against the delivered binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main actor had no child result lifecycle; it proceeded from its own test results to cargo-binary checks and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a completed and consumed handoff; serial had continuous local state, with no lifecycle failure in either run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The delegated child wrote the final files in `/output`, and the parent later inspected the same final file list before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote the whole project itself and listed the non-target output files after cargo-binary checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used child side effects as the final deliverable but without competing writers or overwrite evidence; serial avoided shared-writer state entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child reported clean required differential tests and abort/cargo checks, then the parent spot-checked seven representative oracle cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor ran a larger differential harness, received `ALL TESTS PASSED`, then checked the cargo release binary and file layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed evaluator-aligned oracle checks; serial used a broader local harness, while parallel combined child verification with parent spot checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used one subagent, did not time out, finished in 605.043 agent seconds, and passed the official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used no subagents, did not time out, finished in 934.081 agent seconds, and passed the official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed faster with delegation, serial spent more time in one actor, and neither left budget-pressure symptoms or unfinished work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations are complete and both solutions passed all 39 test cases. The parallel solution succeeded through parent probing, one child implementation, child verification, and parent spot checks; the serial solution succeeded through one continuous actor performing the same categories of work with a broader differential harness. Therefore the observed difference is process structure, not a discordant task outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parent converted oracle probes into a detailed child brief covering thresholds, formatting, CLI parsing, file paths, build commands, and verification.
Child implemented and verified the requested Rust project, and the parent spot-checked the delivered executable before finalizing.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained all oracle findings locally and wrote a modular Cargo project with root binary target and src modules.
Serial actor ran broad differential testing plus cargo-binary spot checks before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a simpler root-level `hopscotch.rs` module; serial used a `src/` library layout with separate formatter and map modules.
Serial tested a wider range of counts in its own harness, while parallel used child verification plus parent spot checks; both satisfied the official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative process contrast only
